data.hypothesis: An 8-output-row tile with 32 contiguous X lanes reduces serial outputs per thread versus the earlier 16- and 32-row variants, while cooperatively initializing all 16 tile rows. It also increases blocks per Y plane and halo loads per output, so this contrasting tile-height/launch-shape experiment tests whether lighter per-thread work offsets lower reuse; no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: This smaller tile tests the observed tradeoff in the same fixed 64-row Y domain.
memory_lessons.claim: The valid 16-row tile measured 3.2230 µs versus the 3.5815 µs baseline, while the valid 32-row variant measured 3.3348 µs. The sample ranges were broad, so the means do not establish a robust tile-height advantage.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Validate this 8-row tile and compare repeated official full-run timings with the baseline and earlier tile variants.

data.notes: The 32-by-8 block loads both halves of the 16-row shared tile before the barrier; the q<0 and q>63 cases wrap by 63 while q=63 remains unchanged. The controller should perform oracle validation, including independent endpoint values, and repeated official timing; this proposal has no new measurements.
transformations: Replace the baseline Y derivative with one shared-memory kernel using 32 contiguous X lanes and an 8-row Y output tile.
Cooperatively load two rows per thread to initialize all 16 shared rows, including four-row halos, and synchronize before evaluating outputs.
Launch blocks of 32 by 8 threads over two X tiles, eight Y tiles, and all 64 z planes.
Preserve the stencil coefficients and expression, full output writes, input/scratch behavior, and exact period-63 boundary mapping that retains in-range index 63.
